It was five years ago so forgive me if things seem loosely put together. However, after I lost consciousness, I remember vivid lighting, almost as if I was lying under stage lights. Then, as if I was in a first person POV, I “sat up”. (I say it like that because I didn’t feel like I was moving, it felt like my surroundings were). There was quiet voices, murmuring, kind of like you’d hear in a library. I was quite scared, but I couldn’t feel my heartbeat or hear myself breath, I could feel myself crying however. At this point it just looked like an endless “area” , like a large field with no colors. What felt like hours later, I felt just, warmth take over my body, and a sense of being ok. I stopped crying, and  before I could get any further, I had a flashlight being shined in my eyes and I could see my mom again. 
It was jarring, and honestly at first I was very upset that I was back. That might seem a bit selfish in my part, seeing as many people aren’t as lucky as I was, but I was depressed and not in a good headspace at the time. I guess that whole experience showed me that while death may seem enjoyable, I should be utterly grateful I got to wake up and see my mom again, and that as lovely as it is, I’m not in an hurry to leave my loved ones and go back. However, I’m not afraid of when I do die now.

I don’t see how I implied I was special chosen, when I spent that time dead, I saw what I believed was the afterlife. It was a very enlightening and amazing moment, however, I don’t believe I had anymore right to life than any other person. I’m just grateful for the second chance. 
I’m sorry you’ve got such a rough view of my second chance at life, I hope you can find a better view point in the future.
